# Language Compatibility

<!-- GENERATED by `npm run gen:lang-compat` from src/core/domains/language/<lang>/capability.ts — DO NOT EDIT. -->

How much to trust tea-rags data **per language**. Each column answers one
question agent must settle before acting on a result:

- **AST chunking** — chunk = source of truth (whole symbol), so `find_symbol`
  suffices, no `Read` needed?
- **Tests chunking** — test chunk a coherent unit (scope / case preserved)?
- **Codegraph** — call-graph signals (`get_callers` / `get_callees` /
  `trace_path` / `fanIn` / `pageRank`) trustworthy for this language?

**Source of truth**: each `src/core/domains/language/<lang>/capability.ts`
descriptor, aggregated by `LanguageFactory.capabilities()`. This file GENERATED
— edit descriptor, run `npm run gen:lang-compat`, never edit here. Per-project
realized numbers live in **prime**, never here.

## Scales — what each tier means for the agent

**AST code chunking** — trust chunk as complete symbol?

- **full** — tree-sitter cuts on real symbol boundaries. Chunk / `find_symbol`
  result IS source of truth; gather code from it, do NOT `Read` to "see the real
  code". `Read` only to MODIFY. (Oversized symbol hard-cap split into `#partN`
  chunks — one part NOT the whole symbol; `find_symbol(symbolId)` reassembles
  every part into one trusted result. See `search-cascade.md` → After-Search
  Navigation.)
- **partial** — chunked by section / heading (Markdown). Section coherent for
  docs; no code symbols to split.
- **none** — CharacterChunker splits at arbitrary offsets; chunk may cut a
  symbol in half. Here `Read` legitimate fallback for exact code.

**Tests code chunking** — trust a test chunk as a unit?

- **high** — test scope (describe / context / it) preserved as chunk (incl.
  injected setup for Ruby).
- **medium** — only function / method boundaries; nesting + setup context lost.
- **low** — test framework unrecognized; chunked as plain functions.
- **N/A** — doc-only.

**Codegraph** — trust call-graph signals?

- Order: **maximum** > **high** > **moderate** > **minimal** > **none**.
- **maximum** — full typed resolution; edges near-complete (YARD-annotated
  Ruby).
- **high** — reliable resolution (typed TS / JS; untyped Ruby's richest chain).
- **moderate** — structural resolution; dynamic-dispatch edges partial — treat
  `fanIn` / callers as a LOWER BOUND, not exhaustive.
- **minimal** — function extraction only, no dispatch.
- **none** — no call graph; codegraph signals absent.

## Realized trust = prime, not this table

This table = **capability ceiling** of the mechanism — static product fact.
Trust you actually get on YOUR index = prime's `resolveSuccessRate` per language
(corpus-dependent). Variance largest for dynamically typed languages: Ruby
**high** untyped, **maximum** YARD-annotated, drops on un-annotated Rails — that
swing is a prime number, not a language property.

**Consequence:** when prime reports low `resolveSuccessRate`, empty
`get_callers` is a resolution artifact, NOT "the symbol has no callers". Do not
conclude absence from a graph the index says is incomplete.

## For humans — resolution tech (not agent-actionable)

- **TypeScript** — 8-strategy chain + ConeDispatch
- **JavaScript** — 6-strategy; CommonJS/ESM require resolution (dynamic gaps)
- **Python** — 6-strategy + ConeDispatch CHA; type hints where present
- **Go** — 6-strategy; explicit interfaces (no poly dispatch)
- **Java** — 6-strategy + java.lang stdlib whitelist + overload disambiguation
- **Rust** — 6-strategy; trait-based dispatch
- **Ruby** — 11-strategy + 4 dispatch components (table/union/cone/dynamic) +
  YARD type-source
- **Bash** — function-call extraction only, no dispatch
- **Markdown** — no call graph
